title: Catching up
goal: Catch up with a friend you haven't seen for a while: say how long it's been, share your news, tell them what you did at the weekend or on holiday, ask 'have you ever…?' and talk about how things have changed.
intro:
Every reunion in Gujarat starts the same way: **ઘણા દિવસે દેખાયો!** 'long time no see!', followed by **બોલ, શું નવાજૂની?** 'so, what's new?'. To answer you need to talk about time: what you did (**ગયો**), what has happened and is still true (**ગયો છે**), what you had done before (**ગયો હતો**), what you were doing when something happened (**કરતો હતો**), and how long it's been (**બે વર્ષ થઈ ગયાં**, **ત્રણ વર્ષથી**, **છ મહિના પહેલાં**).

This unit pulls the past tenses together and adds the small time words that make catching up flow.

grammar.title: Went, has gone, had gone: ગયો, ગયો છે, ગયો હતો
grammar.body:
You know all three forms from unit 16. Catching up is where you need to choose between them.

**Simple past — ગયો, કર્યું** — a finished event, usually with a time word: ગયા મહિને હું દિલ્હી **ગયો** 'I went to Delhi last month'.

**Present perfect — ગયો છે, કર્યું છે** — something that has happened and **still matters now**: news, results, experiences:
નીરવ કૅનેડા **ગયો છે** 'Nirav has gone to Canada' (he's there now)
મારી સગાઈ **થઈ ગઈ છે** 'I've got engaged'
હું બે વાર કેરળ **ગઈ છું** 'I've been to Kerala twice'

**Past perfect — ગયો હતો, કર્યું હતું** — Gujarati uses this much more than English does: for something further back, or a trip that is **over** (you went and came back): ગયા વર્ષે અમે કચ્છ **ગયાં હતાં** 'we went to Kutch last year'. Compare: એ લંડન **ગયો છે** 'he's gone to London (and is there)' vs એ લંડન **ગયો હતો** 'he went to London (and is back)'.

**'Have you ever…?'** is **ક્યારેય** + present perfect: તું **ક્યારેય** ગોવા **ગયો છે**? Answers: **હા, એક વાર**, **બે-ત્રણ વાર**, **ના, ક્યારેય નહીં**, **હજી નહીં**.

Remember the ergative with transitive verbs in all three: **તેં** ક્યારેય ઊંધિયું **ખાધું છે**? — the verb agrees with the object (ઊંધિયું n → ખાધું).

**The trap:** 'I've been to Goa' is **ગયો છું**, not 'ગયો હતો છું', and 'he has gone' (ગયો છે) is not 'he went and came back' (ગયો હતો) — mixing them up sends your friend to the wrong continent.

examples.en: Nirav has gone to London. (he's there now)
Nirav went to London. (and has come back)

grammar.title: Was doing: -તો હતો, and 'I was … when …'
grammar.body:
For something that **was going on** at a moment in the past, use the **-તો** form + **હતો** (both agreeing with the subject), or the **-ઈ રહ્યો હતો** form:

હું જમતો **હતો** = હું જમી **રહ્યો હતો** 'I was eating'
એ સૂતી **હતી** 'she was sleeping'
અમે જોતાં **હતાં** 'we were watching'

**'I was … when …'** — put the background in the -તો હતો form and the event in the simple past, linked by **ત્યારે** (or just **અને** in fast speech):
હું જમતો હતો **ત્યારે** તારો ફોન આવ્યો 'I was eating when your call came'
અમે ટીવી જોતાં હતાં **અને** લાઇટ ગઈ 'we were watching TV and the power went'.

It also describes a period of ongoing activity: આખો મહિનો હું સતત કામ **કરતો હતો** 'I was working non-stop all month'. With **ક્યારનો** it means 'had been doing for ages': હું ક્યારનો ફોન **કરતો હતો**! 'I'd been calling you for ages!'

The same form without હતો is 'used to' (unit 26); context tells them apart.

**The trap:** like 'used to', this form **never** takes the ergative, even with transitive verbs: **હું** ટીવી જોતો હતો, never 'મેં ટીવી જોતો હતો'. Use મેં only with the simple past: **મેં** ટીવી **જોયું**.

grammar.title: For, since and ago: -થી, પહેલાં, થઈ ગયાં
grammar.body:
**Ago** is **પહેલાં** after the time: બે વર્ષ **પહેલાં** 'two years ago', થોડા દિવસ **પહેલાં** 'a few days ago'.

**It's been…** is the time + **થઈ ગયું / ગયા / ગયાં**, agreeing with the time word: ત્રણ મહિના **થઈ ગયા** (મહિના m pl), બે વર્ષ **થઈ ગયાં** (વર્ષ n pl), એક અઠવાડિયું **થઈ ગયું**. 'It's been six months since he left' is **એ ગયો એને છ મહિના થઈ ગયા**.

**For / since** something that is **still going on** is **-થી** + the **present tense**:
હું ત્રણ વર્ષ**થી** અહીં **રહું છું** 'I've been living here for three years'
હું સવાર**થી** ભૂખ્યો **છું** 'I've been hungry since this morning'
Ask with **ક્યારથી?** 'since when / how long?', and use **ત્યારથી** 'ever since then'.

For a period that is **over**, just say the time, with the past: હું ત્યાં બે વર્ષ **રહ્યો** 'I lived there for two years'.

**The trap:** English uses 'have been …ing' and Gujarati uses the plain present: 'I've been learning Gujarati for a year' is **હું એક વર્ષથી ગુજરાતી શીખું છું**, not 'શીખ્યો છું'. And **-થી** with a past event means 'since', not 'ago': 'two years ago' is never 'બે વર્ષથી'.

culture: Catching up in Gujarati is warm and very direct. After **ઘણા દિવસે દેખાયો!** you may hear **ક્યાં ગાયબ હતો?** 'where did you vanish to?', and then questions an English speaker might find personal: how much you earn, when you're getting married (**લગ્ન ક્યારે?**), or that you've put on weight (**જાડો થઈ ગયો!**). None of it is rude — it's interest — and the best answers are cheerful and vague: **ઠીકઠાક**, **ચાલે છે**, **જોઈએ** ('we'll see'). Diwali, Navratri and the December–January wedding season are when **NRG**s (non-resident Gujaratis, from London, Leicester, New Jersey, Toronto or Nairobi) come home, so reunions cluster then, often over tea, a plate of something fried, or at a **ડાયરો**. Friends of the same age switch straight back to **તું**, however long it's been; with a friend's parents, it's **તમે** and **જય શ્રી કૃષ્ણ** as always.

lessons.title: Long time no see!

tip.title: Ago, it's been, for
tip.body:
- 'Ago' = **પહેલાં** after the time: બે વર્ષ **પહેલાં**.
- 'It's been…' = time + **થઈ ગયા / ગયાં**, agreeing: ત્રણ મહિના **થઈ ગયા**, બે વર્ષ **થઈ ગયાં**.
- Still going on: **-થી** + the **present**: હું બે વર્ષથી અહીં **રહું છું**.
tip.pattern: time + પહેલાં · time + થઈ ગયાં · time-થી + present

tip.title: News: the present perfect
tip.body:
- News that's **still true now** takes the perfect: મારી સગાઈ **થઈ ગઈ છે**, મેં નોકરી **બદલી છે**.
- A finished event with a time is plain past: ગયા મહિને નોકરી **મળી**.
- **ગયો છે** = has gone (and is there); **ગયો હતો** = went (and came back).

sentences.roman: bhaṇtar pūruṃ thaī gayuṃ chhe, have nokrī shodhuṃ chhuṃ.
sentences.en: I've finished my studies, now I'm looking for a job.

sentences.native: હા, મેં નોકરી બદલી છે.
sentences.roman: hā, meṃ nokrī badlī chhe.
sentences.en: Yes, I've changed jobs.

sentences.native: મારી બહેનને દીકરો થયો છે!
sentences.roman: mārī bahenne dīkro thayo chhe!
sentences.en: My sister's had a baby boy!

sentences.native: એ લોકો નવા ઘરમાં ગયા છે.
sentences.roman: e loko navā gharmāṃ gayā chhe.
sentences.en: They've moved into a new house.

sentences.native: અંદાજ લગાવ, હું કોને મળી?
sentences.roman: andāj lagāv, huṃ kone maḷī?
sentences.en: Guess who I ran into! (woman)

sentences.native: કામકાજમાં કોઈ ફેરફાર?
sentences.roman: kāmkājmāṃ koī ferfār?
sentences.en: Any changes at work?

sentences.native: તારા ભણતરનું શું થયું?
sentences.roman: tārā bhaṇtarnuṃ shuṃ thayuṃ?
sentences.en: What happened with your studies?

tip.title: Talking about a good time
tip.body:
- A good time: **જલસા કર્યા**, **મજા આવી**, **મજાનો દિવસ હતો**.
- Trips that are over usually take **-યા હતા**: અમે બહારગામ **ગયા હતા**.
- **દરમિયાન** 'during' goes after the noun: વેકેશન **દરમિયાન**.

sentences.native: વીકએન્ડમાં અમે બહારગામ ગયા હતા.
sentences.roman: vīkenḍmāṃ ame bahārgām gayā hatā.
sentences.en: We went out of town at the weekend.

sentences.native: ટ્રિપ કેવી રહી?
sentences.roman: ṭrip kevī rahī?
sentences.en: How was the trip?

sentences.native: બહુ મજાની! ત્રણ દિવસ જલસા કર્યા.
sentences.roman: bahu majānī! traṇ divas jalsā karyā.
sentences.en: Brilliant! We had a ball for three days.

sentences.native: વેકેશન દરમિયાન હું દાદીને ત્યાં રહી.
sentences.roman: vekeshan darmiyān huṃ dādīne tyāṃ rahī.
sentences.en: I stayed at my grandma's during the holidays. (woman)

sentences.native: ડાયરો આખી રાત ચાલ્યો.
sentences.roman: ḍāyro ākhī rāt chālyo.
sentences.en: The dayro went on all night.

sentences.native: રવિવાર બહુ મજાનો હતો.
sentences.roman: ravivār bahu majāno hato.
sentences.en: Sunday was really lovely.

sentences.native: અમે બધા મિત્રો સાથે કચ્છની ટ્રિપ પર ગયા.
sentences.roman: ame badhā mitro sāthe Kachchhnī ṭrip par gayā.
sentences.en: We went on a trip to Kutch with all our friends.

sentences.native: શનિવારે રાત્રે અમે ડાયરામાં ગયા હતા.
sentences.roman: shanivāre rātre ame ḍāyrāmāṃ gayā hatā.
sentences.en: On Saturday night we went to a dayro.

sentences.native: કંઈ ખાસ નહીં, ઘરે જ આરામ કર્યો.
sentences.roman: kaṃī khās nahīṃ, ghare j ārām karyo.
sentences.en: Nothing special, I just relaxed at home.

sentences.native: તેં શનિવારે શું કર્યું?
sentences.roman: teṃ shanivāre shuṃ karyuṃ?
sentences.en: What did you do on Saturday?

tip.title: Have you ever…? ક્યારેય + perfect
tip.body:
- 'Have you ever…?' = **ક્યારેય** + the perfect: તું ક્યારેય ગોવા **ગયો છે**?
- Transitive verbs keep the ergative: **તેં** ક્યારેય ઢોકળાં **ખાધાં છે**? (agrees with ઢોકળાં)
- Answers: **હા, એક વાર** · **બે-ત્રણ વાર** · **ના, ક્યારેય નહીં** · **હજી નહીં**.

sentences.native: તું ક્યારેય મુંબઈ ગઈ છે?
sentences.roman: tuṃ kyārey Mumbaī gaī chhe?
sentences.en: Have you ever been to Mumbai? (to a woman)

sentences.native: તેં ક્યારેય ઢોકળાં ખાધાં છે?
sentences.roman: teṃ kyārey ḍhokḷāṃ khādhāṃ chhe?
sentences.en: Have you ever had dhokla?

sentences.native: હા, બે-ત્રણ વાર ખાધાં છે.
sentences.roman: hā, be-traṇ vār khādhāṃ chhe.
sentences.en: Yes, I've had them two or three times.

sentences.native: મેં ક્યારેય ટ્રેકિંગ નથી કર્યું.
sentences.roman: meṃ kyārey ṭreking nathī karyuṃ.
sentences.en: I've never been trekking.

sentences.native: તમે ક્યારેય ગરબા રમ્યા છો?
sentences.roman: tame kyārey garbā ramyā chho?
sentences.en: Have you ever danced garba?

sentences.native: હું એક વાર કેરળ ગઈ છું, બહુ સુંદર છે.
sentences.roman: huṃ ek vār Keraḷ gaī chhuṃ, bahu sundar chhe.
sentences.en: I've been to Kerala once, it's beautiful. (woman)

sentences.native: મેં હજી સુધી પાણીપૂરી નથી ખાધી!
sentences.roman: meṃ hajī sudhī pāṇīpūrī nathī khādhī!
sentences.en: I still haven't had pani puri!

sentences.native: તેં ક્યારેય ગુજરાતી ફિલ્મ જોઈ છે?
sentences.roman: teṃ kyārey gujarātī film joī chhe?
sentences.en: Have you ever seen a Gujarati film?

sentences.native: આ નવું કૅફે અજમાવીએ?
sentences.roman: ā navuṃ kefe ajmāvīe?
sentences.en: Shall we try this new café?

sentences.native: ના, ક્યારેય નહીં, પણ જોવી છે.
sentences.roman: nā, kyārey nahīṃ, paṇ jovī chhe.
sentences.en: No, never, but I'd like to.

tip.title: Was doing: -તો હતો
tip.body:
- 'Was doing' = **-તો હતો** (or **-ઈ રહ્યો હતો**), both parts agreeing: હું જમતો **હતો**, એ જમતી **હતી**.
- 'I was … when …': background in -તો હતો, then **ત્યારે** + the event: હું નહાતી હતી **ત્યારે** ફોન આવ્યો.
- No ergative: **હું** ટીવી જોતો હતો.

sentences.native: તું કાલે રાત્રે શું કરતો હતો?
sentences.roman: tuṃ kāle rātre shuṃ karto hato?
sentences.en: What were you up to last night?

sentences.native: હું નહાતી હતી ત્યારે તારો ફોન આવ્યો.
sentences.roman: huṃ nahātī hatī tyāre tāro fon āvyo.
sentences.en: I was in the shower when you called. (woman)

sentences.native: અમે જમતાં હતાં અને અચાનક મહેમાન આવ્યા.
sentences.roman: ame jamtāṃ hatāṃ ane achānak mahemān āvyā.
sentences.en: We were having dinner and suddenly guests turned up.

sentences.native: આખો મહિનો હું સતત કામ કરતો હતો.
sentences.roman: ākho mahino huṃ satat kām karto hato.
sentences.en: I was working non-stop all month.

sentences.native: તું ક્યાં હતો? હું તને ક્યારનો ફોન કરતો હતો!
sentences.roman: tuṃ kyāṃ hato? huṃ tane kyārno fon karto hato!
sentences.en: Where were you? I'd been calling you for ages!

sentences.native: એ લોકો ક્યાં જતા હતા?
sentences.roman: e loko kyāṃ jatā hatā?
sentences.en: Where were they going?

sentences.native: હું લંડનમાં હતી ત્યારે અમદાવાદને બહુ મિસ કરતી હતી.
sentences.roman: huṃ Landanmāṃ hatī tyāre Amdāvādne bahu mis kartī hatī.
sentences.en: When I was in London I really missed Ahmedabad. (woman)

sentences.native: અમને બધાંને તારી બહુ યાદ આવતી હતી.
sentences.roman: amne badhāṃne tārī bahu yād āvtī hatī.
sentences.en: We all missed you so much.

sentences.native: હું દોડતો હતો અને પડી ગયો.
sentences.roman: huṃ doḍto hato ane paḍī gayo.
sentences.en: I was running and I fell over.

sentences.native: હમણાં હમણાં હું રોજ સવારે દોડવા જાઉં છું.
sentences.roman: hamṇāṃ hamṇāṃ huṃ roj savāre doḍvā jāuṃ chhuṃ.
sentences.en: Lately I've been going for a run every morning.

tip.title: Changes, and since when
tip.body:
- **બદલાવું** 'to change' (become different): તું **બદલાઈ ગયો** છે.
- વજન **વધ્યું / ઘટ્યું** 'put on / lost weight' — વજન is neuter.
- **ક્યારથી?** 'since when?' and **ત્યારથી** 'ever since' go with the **present** for things still going on: ક્યારથી જીમ **જાય છે**?

sentences.native: તું તો બહુ બદલાઈ ગયો છે!
sentences.roman: tuṃ to bahu badlāī gayo chhe!
sentences.en: You've really changed! (to a man)

sentences.native: તું ક્યારથી જીમ જાય છે?
sentences.roman: tuṃ kyārthī jīm jāy chhe?
sentences.en: How long have you been going to the gym?

sentences.native: છ મહિનાથી જાઉં છું, પાંચ કિલો વજન ઘટ્યું છે.
sentences.roman: chha mahināthī jāuṃ chhuṃ, pāṃch kilo vajan ghaṭyuṃ chhe.
sentences.en: Six months now, I've lost five kilos.

sentences.native: લગ્ન પછી મારું વજન વધી ગયું.
sentences.roman: lagna pachhī māruṃ vajan vadhī gayuṃ.
sentences.en: I put on weight after the wedding.

sentences.native: નવી નોકરી મળી ત્યારથી એ બહુ બિઝી છે.
sentences.roman: navī nokrī maḷī tyārthī e bahu bizī chhe.
sentences.en: He's been really busy ever since he got the new job.

sentences.native: અમદાવાદ પણ બહુ બદલાઈ ગયું છે, મેટ્રો આવી ગઈ!
sentences.roman: Amdāvād paṇ bahu badlāī gayuṃ chhe, meṭro āvī gaī!
sentences.en: Ahmedabad's changed a lot too, there's a metro now!

sentences.native: તમે અહીં ક્યારથી રહો છો?
sentences.roman: tame ahīṃ kyārthī raho chho?
sentences.en: How long have you lived here?

sentences.native: ભાવ કેટલા વધી ગયા છે!
sentences.roman: bhāv keṭlā vadhī gayā chhe!
sentences.en: Prices have gone up so much!

sentences.native: તું પહેલાં કરતાં વધારે ખુશ દેખાય છે.
sentences.roman: tuṃ pahelāṃ kartāṃ vadhāre khush dekhāy chhe.
sentences.en: You look happier than before.

sentences.native: તું હજી પણ એવી જ છે!
sentences.roman: tuṃ hajī paṇ evī j chhe!
sentences.en: You're still exactly the same! (to a woman)
